## Context / Problem
Pydantic AI 1.107 emits `pydantic_ai._warnings.PydanticAIDeprecationWarning` when `infer_model("openai:<model>")` constructs a model: in v2 the ambiguous prefix will switch from Chat Completions to Responses. A pinned-environment runtime probe captured that exact category and message. Rebar currently relies on Chat Completions for hosted OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so leaving the ambiguous prefix would silently change the wire contract on upgrade. The operator approved preserving Chat Completions with `openai-chat:`; story `upbeat-illadvised-springtail` owns the eventual deliberate Responses migration.

## Approach
Normalize every rebar-composed or legacy `openai:` Pydantic AI model target to the explicit `openai-chat:` qualifier at the shared primary and model-class/fallback resolution seams. In `_pai_model`, normalize the explicitly-qualified early-return branch as well as inferred targets. In `_resolve_target`, treat configured providers `openai` and `openai-chat` as aliases of one provider family before the existing conflict decision: every combination of those two configured/inline spellings resolves canonically to `openai-chat:`, while all cross-family conflicts continue to raise unchanged. Update both independent ProviderSession gates: the cfg.base_url builder registration and the per-candidate endpoint-override guard must recognize `openai-chat`, so local OpenAI-compatible endpoints keep their provider/profile override. Preserve other provider qualifiers unchanged and document `openai-chat:` as the supported Chat Completions spelling.

## Scope
- Update `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` so both `_pai_model`'s colon-bearing early return and inferred OpenAI targets normalize to `openai-chat:`.
- Update `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` so configured `openai`/`openai-chat` provider aliases and inline `openai:`/`openai-chat:` qualifiers compare as one family before the conflict guard, producing canonical `openai-chat:` for primary and fallback targets without weakening cross-family conflict rejection.
- Update both `openai`-keyed gates in `src/rebar/llm/providers.py`: cfg.base_url builder registration and the per-candidate endpoint-override guard.
- Strengthen provider-resolution, custom-endpoint, fallback, library-contract, and provider-matrix tests in `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py`, `tests/unit/test_openai_compatible_provider.py`, `tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py`, `tests/unit/test_model_classes.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py`, and `tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py`.
- Update canonical operator/developer examples in `.github/llm-providers/openai.toml`, `docs/llm-framework.md`, `docs/llm-example-configs.md`, `docs/workflow-authoring-v2.md`, `docs/reuse-surface.md`, the model examples in `src/rebar/llm/config.py` and `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py`, and their packaged `src/rebar/schemas/workflow.v{1,2,3}.schema.json` descriptions. Refresh the v1/v2 non-semantic golden hashes in `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_schema_golden.py`.
- Keep legacy `openai:` spellings in tests that explicitly prove backward-compatible normalization.
- The nine `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/*.eval.yaml` grader strings are out of scope: current `run_eval` executes only deterministic scorers and never constructs those report-only grader models, so they cannot emit this warning; the deliberate Responses migration story can revisit them if an executable judge path is added.

## Testing
- The held-out oracle imports `PydanticAIDeprecationWarning` from `pydantic_ai._warnings` and promotes it to error around real `infer_model` calls for inferred, explicit, custom-endpoint, and fallback paths. Before repair, `infer_model("openai:gpt-4o")` was observed RED with the exact warning; after repair, every rebar-resolved target constructs without it.
- Parameterize configured `openai`/`openai-chat` against inline `openai:`/`openai-chat:` and require all four combinations to resolve canonically without a spurious conflict; retain a non-OpenAI cross-family conflict control that must raise.
- Run real loopback custom-endpoint tests and provider/fallback parity tests to prove Chat Completions payloads, endpoint routing, and structured-output profile behavior are preserved.
- Run the live-provider overlay contract and workflow schema golden tests so canonical examples accept `openai-chat:` and the description-only schema hashes are deliberate.
- Sweep the focused tests with the exact warning category promoted to error, then run repository lint and typecheck.
- Search canonical examples for ambiguous `openai:` spellings while excluding intentional legacy-compatibility tests and report-only eval graders.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Inferred OpenAI targets resolve to `openai-chat:`; verified by provider-resolution tests.
- [ ] Legacy-explicit `openai:` targets resolve to `openai-chat:`; verified by interface tests.
- [ ] Primary and fallback model-class targets resolve to `openai-chat:`; verified by model-class tests.
- [ ] Configured `openai`/`openai-chat` and inline `openai:`/`openai-chat:` are treated as one provider family and canonically resolve without a spurious conflict.
- [ ] Cross-family provider conflicts and non-OpenAI target behavior remain unchanged.
- [ ] Real model construction emits no `pydantic_ai._warnings.PydanticAIDeprecationWarning` with that exact category promoted to error.
- [ ] Loopback custom endpoints still receive Chat Completions payloads; verified by real-seam provider tests.
- [ ] The custom-endpoint profile override remains active on cfg.base_url and per-candidate endpoint paths.
- [ ] Canonical operator/developer examples and provider-matrix contracts use `openai-chat:` for Chat Completions.
- [ ] Description-only schema changes have deliberately refreshed golden hashes.
- [ ] Focused tests pass.
- [ ] Repository lint passes.
- [ ] Repository typecheck passes.
